classification.difficultyReason: Write the relationship for right-angled triangles with algebraic labels. One part uses vertex names and one has a numeric side with an unknown. Just above direct substitution.

content.prompt:
Write an equation describing the relationship between the sides of these right-angled triangles.

$\text{side}^{2}+\text{side}^{2}=\text{hypotenuse}^{2}$

answer.worked:
The side opposite the right angle is $m$.
$$k^{2}+l^{2}=m^{2}$$

The hypotenuse is $DF$, opposite the right angle at $E$.
$$DE^{2}+EF^{2}=DF^{2}$$

The side opposite the right angle is $15$.
$$9^{2}+y^{2}=15^{2}$$
